newsitem.title: USA: The Hartford launches new AARP business.
newsitem.headline: The Hartford launches new AARP business.

text.p: Diversified insurer The Hartford said Thursday it has signed a 10-year contract with the American Association of Retired Persons (AARP) to provide customer and telemarketing services for AARP's group health insurance program.
The contract will take effect on Jan. 1 of next year, the Hartford said.
AARP's group health program had been provided by Prudential Insurance since 1981.
The Hartford said it plans to offer jobs to 1,600 Prudential employees, who currently support customer service functions for the program, in Fort Washington, Allentown and Montgomery, Pa.

Under the contract, the Hartford will provide information on AARP's group health program to interested members, enroll members in the program and handle telemarketing services and member services, including the customer service call center, billing, collection and information distribution.
The Hartford will not provide any group health insurance products.
AARP's group health insurance program serves 5.7 million members.

"What's significant about this is that we are developing a new business, based on some capabilities we developed through servicing our AARP auto and homeowners insurance customers," The Hartford spokeswoman Connie Gurney told Reuters.
The Hartford writes about $1.2 billion in annual premium through the AARP auto and homeowners insurance program, in a contract which runs through 2002.
